content.name: p
children: The diff/apply behavior is shared with the CLI. The operator is not a separate implementation of role management logic; it is a controller wrapped around the same core engine.

content.name: p
children: Multiple policies may target the same database only if their ownership claims are disjoint.

content.name: p
children: The controller derives ownership claims from declared roles and schema/profile expansions, then rejects overlapping policies by setting conflict status instead of letting policies revoke each other's grants.

children: Reconciliation is serialized per database target in two layers:

children.name: li
children: in-process locking to prevent concurrent reconciles in one operator replica

children.name: li
children: PostgreSQL advisory locking to prevent concurrent reconciles across replicas

content.name: p
children: This is the core safety boundary for production use. It ensures one database target has one active inspect/diff/apply cycle at a time.

content.name: p
children: The controller uses different retry behavior depending on failure class:

children.name: li
children: invalid specs and ownership conflicts: normal reconcile interval

children.name: li
children: secret-missing and other non-transient configuration errors: normal reconcile interval

children.name: li
children: transient infrastructure/database failures: exponential backoff with jitter

children.name: li
children: lock contention: short dedicated retry path

content.name: p
children: That keeps the operator from hammering the Kubernetes API or the database during persistent misconfiguration.
